source.title: AND: Audio Network Dissection for Interpreting Deep Acoustic Models
source.authors: Tung-Yu Wu; Yu-Xiang Lin; T. Weng

record.tranche_reason: Measures neuron polysemanticity in audio models using a caption-clustering criterion, a different method from the original vision-focused studies.
record.gate_note: The study's own neuron-interpretability results in Section 4.5 and Appendix G.3 bear on training-strategy and measurement dependence. The cited vision and language findings are not rows. Other experiments evaluate dissection quality, pruning, or acoustic feature importance rather than the versions recorded here.
record.test_reason: Section 4.5 and Appendix G measure the share of 'uninterpretable' (polysemantic) neurons per transformer block in three audio models trained differently. This is a new setting (audio transformers), with results on whether the share depends on training (V5) and on the measurement threshold (V7).
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that supervised training narrows neuron attention with depth, while self-supervised pretraining keeps neurons diverse/polysemantic. They also report that the percentages shift with τ and top-K but the trends hold.
record.recipe_differences: Uses audio captions, language-model summaries, and sentence clustering to assess acoustic neurons; it does not reproduce the original vision-neuron measurements.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported polysemantic-neuron percentage varies with the clustering threshold τ and the number of highly activated samples top-K; the authors report similar trends across those settings.

fits_no_version.finding: A substantial share of neurons in audio transformers is classified as uninterpretable by the caption-clustering criterion (figure-only). On GTZAN, at most 20% are uninterpretable at τ=4.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Polysemantic neurons are common in audio transformer classifiers, at rates that depend on the dataset.

fits_no_version.finding: The average number of acoustic adjectives per neuron decreases with depth in AST, is mitigated in BEATs-finetuned, and is flat and lower in BEATs-frozen (Fig 5). The authors read this as narrowing polysemanticity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Description breadth per neuron, as a proxy for polysemanticity, varies with training strategy.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), Proceedings of the 41st International Conference on Machine Learning, PMLR 235, 2024
record.problems: Polysemanticity is operationalized through clustering sentences in audio captions and a threshold, rather than an independent ground truth for neuron meaning. Core percentages are presented in figures without exact values in the text. The reported training-strategy comparison does not isolate training strategy from all other model differences or test the performance cost of reducing polysemanticity.
record.rows_left_out: No additional rows from Sections 4.1–4.4: those results concern dissection accuracy, human ratings, pruning, and feature importance rather than the tested versions.

untested.parts: Activation function (SoLU), architecture swaps holding training fixed, regularization, and whether lowering polysemanticity costs performance. AST vs BEATs also differ in architecture and pretraining, so training strategy is not isolated.
Which part of the activation range is examined (only top-K highest are used), and alternative explanation-scoring methods.
No initialization, regularization or noise test under sufficient capacity.
No re-examination of canonical polysemantic neurons.

missing.what: GTZAN replication. At most 20% of neurons are uninterpretable at τ=4. At τ=5 the trend is clearer: BEATs-frozen stays diverse and AST concentrates with depth.

record.verdict_notes: Polysemanticity is operationalized as failure of top-K SALMONN captions to share a K-means cluster (11 clusters). Caption noise or cluster granularity could inflate the counts. All key values are figure-only. Tranche changed from T2 to T3 because the domain (audio) is new, not just the method.

versions.untested_parts: No image-classifier neurons or the cited InceptionV1 neuron are tested.
No transformer language-model neurons or language-token/context polysemanticity are tested.
The study does not test whether polysemanticity is caused by representing more features than there are neurons.
Initialization, regularization, and training noise as causes under sufficient capacity are not tested.
The study compares training strategies, but does not test activation-function changes, SoLU, modern convnets, or whether polysemanticity can be reduced without a large performance loss.
It does not test whether canonical vision or language polysemantic neurons share a single underlying feature or job.
It varies the number of highly activated samples and the clustering threshold, but does not compare activation-range portions or alternative explanation-scoring methods.

rows.subject: AST
rows.stage_stated: AudioSet supervised pretraining; ESC50 supervised training of all layers
rows.operation_detail: Classified neurons as interpretable or uninterpretable by clustering audio-description sentences and applying threshold τ=4.
rows.measure: Percentage of neurons classified as uninterpretable (polysemantic) by the study's clustering criterion.
rows.value: figure only; the text states the percentage decreases from shallow to deep blocks
rows.note: The authors interpret this as neurons narrowing their attention during supervised training.
rows.check: Subject and condition are fine. The value is figure-only. 'Uninterpretable' means fewer than τ of the top-5 captions share a K-means cluster. This is a proxy for polysemanticity, not a direct measure.

rows.subject: BEATs-finetuned
rows.stage_stated: AudioSet self-supervised pretraining; ESC50 supervised fine-tuning of all layers
rows.operation_detail: Classified neurons as interpretable or uninterpretable by clustering audio-description sentences and applying threshold τ=4.
rows.measure: Percentage of neurons classified as uninterpretable (polysemantic) by the study's clustering criterion.
rows.value: figure only; the text says the diverse-to-accordant trend is mitigated compared with AST
rows.note: The authors describe supervised fine-tuning of the whole pretrained model as guiding attention to converge, but less strongly than for AST.
rows.check: Not a weaker effect. BEATs-finetuned is one arm of the training-strategy contrast and shows its own distinct layer-wise pattern (the trend is mitigated relative to AST). Mark observed as part of the contrast, not partial.

source_check.correct: Figure only. For Fig 6 the text says only that full-model fine-tuning of BEATs guides attention to converge in deeper layers by narrowing neurons' responsive features. It makes no comparison with AST. The phrase 'diverse-to-accordant trend is mitigated' describes average adjectives per neuron (Sec 4.4, Fig 5), not the share of uninterpretable neurons.
source_check.locator_found: Sec 4.5 Results (Fig 6); the 'mitigated' wording is in Sec 4.4 about Fig 5
source_check.problem: The qualitative description comes from another metric (adjective counts, Fig 5), not from Fig 6's share of uninterpretable neurons.

rows.note: The authors describe this model as showing diverse abilities associated with self-supervised pretraining.
rows.check: A flat layer profile (p > 0.05 in the Fig 5 legend) is the contrast condition showing the share depends on training. It is not evidence against V5, so partial is wrong.

relationships.condition: AST (supervised), BEATs-finetuned, BEATs-frozen (SSL) on ESC50, τ=4, top-5
relationships.reason: The layer-wise share of uninterpretable neurons differs by training strategy: it falls with depth in AST, the fall is mitigated in BEATs-finetuned, and it is flat in BEATs-frozen (r1–r3, Fig 6).
relationships.display_finding: The share of uninterpretable neurons fell with depth in AST, fell less in fine-tuned BEATs, and stayed flat across layers in frozen BEATs.

tranche.reason: A new setting (audio transformers) with results on how the share of uninterpretable neurons depends on training strategy and on the measurement threshold.

source_check.notes: All values are figure only. 'Uninterpretable' means fewer than τ of the top-K descriptions share a K-means sentence cluster, which is a proxy for polysemanticity. The GTZAN replication (App G.4, Fig 14) is not in the rows: at most 20% uninterpretable at τ=4, and at τ=5 AST concentrates while BEATs-frozen stays diverse. ESC50 accuracy is 95.0/89.75/84.75% (AST/BEATs-finetuned/BEATs-frozen).

statements.correction: ESC50, τ=4, top-5, Fig 6 (figure only). AST: the share of uninterpretable neurons decreases from shallow to deep blocks. BEATs-finetuned: full-model supervised fine-tuning narrows neurons' responsive features in deeper layers, with no comparison to AST stated. BEATs-frozen: the share is consistent across layers. 'Diverse-to-accordant trend is mitigated' in BEATs-finetuned is said of adjective counts (Fig 5).
statements.problem: The statement says the fall with depth is 'mitigated in BEATs-finetuned' for the share of uninterpretable neurons. The text says 'mitigated' only for average adjectives per neuron (Sec 4.4, Fig 5). Fig 6 values cannot be read.

statements.correction: Table 1 settings. AST: supervised pretraining on AudioSet, then supervised fine-tuning of all layers on ESC50. BEATs-finetuned: SSL pretraining, then supervised fine-tuning of all layers. BEATs-frozen: SSL pretraining, then only the final linear layer trained. Only the AST vs BEATs contrast also varies the model (architecture), which the text does not discuss. BEATs-finetuned vs BEATs-frozen has the same model and pretraining, and their layer profiles still differ (narrowing in deeper layers vs flat).
statements.problem: The confound is the cataloguer's caveat, not a result in the text. V5 counts both architecture and training as levers, so the confound does not qualify V5, and limits_scope is wrong for this study. The statement is also overbroad. Pretraining objective (supervised vs SSL) is the training strategy the paper compares. BEATs-finetuned vs BEATs-frozen keeps architecture and pretraining fixed.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The study reports different layer-wise polysemanticity patterns across training strategies, with AST decreasing across depth and the decrease mitigated for BEATs-finetuned (r1, r2).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: BEATs-frozen is reported as consistent across layers, and the study does not establish that reducing polysemanticity has no large performance cost (r3).
